description: Curated static-research queues for game systems not yet represented by a verified SoD2SE capability. Native names are candidate registration names only; they are not runtime hooks or confirmed API contracts.

domains.summary: Ambient population, special-zombie spawn weights, custom spawn requests, hordes, and siege waves.
asset_observations: String scanning of the supplied cooked assets found spawn entries, population caps, spawn weights, cooldowns, and special-zombie classes in DefaultAmbientSpawnSetup/MGR_AmbientSpawner assets.
AllZombieTypes contains readable names for Bloater, Feral, Juggernaut, and Screamer; this does not prove the full classification schema or editable asset pipeline.
mod_opportunities: Configurable special-infected frequency or horde composition.
A campaign spawn-pressure preset that adjusts population and cooldown settings.
questions: Which values are authoritative per difficulty, map, and game mode, and which are only UI queries?
How do the ambient spawner, mission-forced spawns, plague-heart spawns, and siege waves interact?
Which calls are server-authoritative, and how are active-spawn limits and cleanup enforced?
promotion_requirements: Resolve owner classes, parameter metadata, and the call/dispatch paths for each candidate.
Map difficulty and game-mode selection plus spawn lifetime and cleanup rules.
Build offline model tests before considering a runtime capability.

domains.summary: Fuel, engine/frame condition, repair/refuel requests, vehicle damage zones, and occupancy events.
asset_observations: The supplied vehicle assets contain readable fields and symbols for engine, frame, gas-tank, zone health, repair items, and vehicle interaction.
mod_opportunities: Optional vehicle fuel use, durability, or repair-cost settings.
Vehicle information and condition display, if an established game UI extension point is found.
questions: Which component owns condition and fuel values, and when are they replicated or saved?
Do server request functions mutate state directly or validate inventory, range, and repair items first?
How do vehicle explosions, zone damage, and mission-spawned vehicle defaults differ?
promotion_requirements: Confirm object ownership, parameter layouts, authority checks, and save/replication behavior.
Keep vehicle requests inside original validation paths; do not write guessed offsets.
Create boundary and failure-path tests for fuel, repair, and destroyed vehicles.

domains.summary: Inventory queries, equipped gear, rucksacks, item counts, and weapon durability.
asset_observations: The current 1100-asset export has adjacent consumable and locker/UI assets but no complete inventory asset family; absence from this partial export is not evidence that the game lacks those assets.
mod_opportunities: Inventory quality-of-life features, provided item transfer and save semantics are verified.
questions: Which item operations preserve stack, ownership, weight, and replication invariants?
Which durability paths cover melee hits, ranged shots, jamming, and repair items?
When are inventory change callbacks fired for local prediction versus authoritative updates?
promotion_requirements: Map item instance and container identity without retaining raw UObject pointers.
Trace the authoritative mutation path and the matching save/replication notifications.
Test duplicate requests, empty stacks, equipment swaps, and interrupted transactions.

domains.summary: Facility slots and tasks, morale/resources, outpost claims, upgrades, and base-data replication.
asset_observations: BaseManagementUI strings expose facility build/upgrade/mod actions, resource and morale sections, and outpost slots. These strings establish UI concepts, not safe mutation points.
mod_opportunities: Configurable facility production, upkeep, morale effects, or outpost yield.
A base-planning quality-of-life feature that reports resource sources and facility effects.
questions: Where are production, upkeep, and morale effects calculated and aggregated?
How do facility task start/end, facility upgrade, and base migration affect cached resources?
Which outpost checks are eligibility rules versus resource-state mutations?
promotion_requirements: Trace the full state transition from UI request through authority validation to save update.
Keep player-base changes separate from NPC enclaves and mission bases.
Test resource totals, concurrent facility tasks, and map/community transitions.

domains.summary: Mission creation/completion/failure, enclave identity and relationships, recruitment records, and community events.
asset_observations: The supplied mission/enclave assets identify campaign and relationship concepts. Their readable names do not establish mission completion safety or permanent character identity.

Full-package bytecode search finds seven serialized InitializeEvent calls from event factory functions, but no serialized call token for FinishConditionCheck, SendMissionToState, or state outcome notifications; native/reflected dispatch remains possible.
mod_opportunities: Mission and enclave quality-of-life settings, such as clearer status or configurable cooldowns.
Recruitment and relationship assistance that preserves original mission and eligibility checks.
questions: How are mission IDs and enclave IDs kept stable across map travel and save/load?
Which mission callbacks fire once, and which are replicated or replayed during restore?
How do recruit records become live survivor objects and enter the player's community?
promotion_requirements: Confirm one-shot event semantics, authoritative side, and transition ordering.
Trace mission/enclave IDs through save and load without using display names as identity.
Test cancellation, failure, completion, map travel, and repeated callback delivery.

limitations: A registered name plus an RVA proves only a static name-to-code mapping for the target executable.
The asset export is a partial 1100-file tree; asset-path matches and string scans do not prove a complete content inventory or an editable/cookable pipeline.
No candidate domain is enabled in Game API or consumed by a gameplay plugin until its owner, signature, authority, lifetime, and tests are established.
